review_candidates.title: Project Manager HCI
review_candidates.description: Company Description Founded in 1961, WWF works to help people and nature thrive. As a global conservation organization, WWF operates in more than 100 countries, partnering with communities, companies, and governments to protect wildlife, conserve vital habitats, and advance sustainable solutions. Grounded in science and driven by collaboration, WWF works to help nature by conserving biodiversity, supporting resilient communities, and addressing climate change. Nearly 1 million people in the United States and more than 5 million globally are WWF members. Project Description The Heart of Conservation Initiative ( HCI ) is a 5-year global project designed to address systemic barriers that limit Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ ability to steward their lands, territories, waters, and biodiversity-rich ecosystems. Despite strong evidence that Indigenous Peoples and local communities manage or influence at least 37% of remaining natural lands globally, they receive less than 1% of international climate and biodiversity finance, face complex donor procedures, limited direct access to funding, and insufficient recognition in decision-making arenas. Building on the achievements of the GEF-7 Inclusive Conservation Initiative (ICI), HCI’s objective is to increase Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ organizational capacities and ability to access sustainable finance at scale for territorial stewardship to deliver social, economic, cultural, and Global Environmental Benefits. The project is transformative in that it targets structural change in biodiversity finance systems—shifting from centralized, intermediary-driven models toward more inclusive, Indigenous Peoples and local community-led financing and governance mechanisms. This will be achieved through four integrated components: (i) organizational and technical self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community funds and organizations and implementation of self-determined Indigenous Peoples- and local community-led sub-projects across Latin America, Africa, and Asia; (ii) collective self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community-led funds and organizations’ institutional, fiduciary, and technical capacities; (iii) enhancing Indigenous Peoples' and local communities’ representation and influence in global biodiversity and biodiversity finance processes; and (iv) advancing knowledge, learning, and evidence on rights-based, inclusive conservation. Job Description Major Function The Project Manager will lead the GCU’s support for the HCI partners and ensure successful delivery of all components. They will supervise staff in a Global Coordination Unit (GCU), provide day-to-day management of the project and, with support from the Partner Liaison, coordinate with ten (10) Component 1 Partners, and partners and specialists in Components 2 through 5. This is a unique role managing and representing a global, Indigenous-led project that should respond both to Indigenous Peoples and local community partners’ priorities as well as meet GEF requirements. The Project Manager will report to the Senior Director, Conservation Areas, and Senior Director, Inclusive Conservation (Project Co-Leads) Key Responsibilities Technical Delivery of Project Components: Component 1: Work with Component 1 partners to review and approve their annual work plans and budgets, provide technical inputs to their on-the-ground work, as needed, and support their self-strengthening plans. Component 2: Lead and coordinate delivery of Component 2 with GCU staff support; Work with Component 1 partners to identify common capacity-strengthening needs and develop and implement a collective strengthening program. Component 3: Lead and coordinate delivery of Component 3 with GCU staff support; Design and implement the Youth Policy Leaders program and work with Component 1 and 2 partners to identify policy processes and to enable effective, HCI-supported engagement therein. Support GCU staff to ensure successful delivery of Components 4 and 5. Project Management: Day-to-day management, monitoring, and evaluation of project activities and results as outlined in the CERDoc, Grant Agreement, and Annual Work Plan and Budget to achieve the project objective and targets in the Results Framework. Responsibilities will include, but not be limited to: Ensure that the GCU holds regular virtual meetings with Component 1 (C1) partners and as required with additional partners involved in the other components, Manage the workflow for the Indigenous Global Steering Committee (IGSC), in collaboration with the Project Co-Leads. In collaboration with all project sub-grantees and partners, develop the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) for the global HCI for each project year, for no-objection from the WWF GEF Agency and approval by the IGSC. Share C1 Partners’ annual workplans and budgets for no-objection from WWF GEF Agency and for IGSC information. Provide high-level oversight and monitoring of procurement and expenditure in line with the AWPB in collaboration with the Finance and Operations (FO) Manager. Review progress of work plan and monitoring plan in collaboration with the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer. Responsible for organization of inception workshop and other critical project workshops and meetings. Manage the design and maintenance of a project website, and the development and implementation of a communications strategy in collaboration with the Communications and Knowledge Management (CKM) Officer. Provide support for project implementation support and learning visits and internal and external reviews/evaluations with relevant GCU staff. Support the MEL Officer to organize annual reflection workshops to identify lessons learned and propose potential changes for adaptive management to ensure project results and indicator targets are reached. Troubleshoot with GCU staff, component partners and Project co-leads to address challenges and create enabling conditions for trusting partnerships and project success. Maintain a project risk register, including identification of risks to project success and development of mitigation measures in coordination with C1 partners and other project partners. Prepare and execute a project exit plan, including hand-off of project equipment and resources, close of grants and agreements, consultations and communications with project partners and interested parties, and ensure sustainability of project results. Champion the promise and achievements of the project, elevating its contributions to systems change and Indigenous Peoples and local community-led partners whenever possible. Any other tasks that are relevant to the assignment. Staff management: Supervise the GCU staff including MEL Officer (crosscutting, especially components 1, 4 and 5), FO Manager (crosscutting), Environmental and Social Safeguards Officer (crosscutting, especially component 1), Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Officer (crosscutting , especially component 1), CKM Officer (crosscutting, especially components 2 and 4), Logistics and Administrative Assistant (crosscutting), and any other directly recruited staff or consultants. Prepare TORs to recruit consultants, staff and sub-contracts in consultation with Project Co-Leads and for no-objection from WWF GEF Agency. Reporting: Collaborate with the MEL Officer to aggregate information from Component 1 Partner sub-projects and formulate semi-annual Project Progress Reports and ensure timely delivery to the WWF GEF Agency. Prepare workshop reports following the inception and other critical project workshops. Collaborate with the FO Manager to oversee the preparation and disbursement of sub-grants to Component 1 partners and grants and agreements under the other 4 components. Collaborate with the FO Manager to aggregate financial information from C1 Partners and oversee the development of quarterly financial reports and ensure timely delivery to the WWF GEF Agency. Collaborate with the WWF network and partners to ensure co-finance reporting on a yearly basis. Prepare a Project Close Report. Quality Assurance: Provide quality assurance for project activities, including sub-grants. Provide quality assurance through review of reports and other products from partners, technical specialists, consultants, and staff. Ensure implementation in line with the GEF and WWF standards and policies. Week-long, international travel may be expected on approximately a quarterly basis. Partnerships: Coordinate with co-financed projects and liaise with project partners to ensure co-financing commitments are realized. Attract additional partners and co-financing. Ensure smooth coordination and communication among all project partners, and with the Component 1 partners (the latter in collaboration with Partner Liaison). Manage stakeholder engagement and ensure gender and social inclusion considerations are fully integrated throughout project implementation in collaboration with the Social and Environmental Safeguards (ESS) and Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) Officers. Represent the project at conferences, meetings, and workshops. Qualifications Key Competencies Strategic Collaboration and Leadership. Able to lead and influence large and highly dispersed teams and coalitions, dealing with risk mitigation and conflict management. Intercultural and adaptive management skills Results-oriented project management Collaboration Cross-cultural communication Skills And Abilities 10 years of technical working experience, including at least five years of project management experience. Bachelor’s Degree; post-graduate degree in a relevant field preferred. At least five years’ experience supporting and working in solidarity with Indigenous people and local community organizations, and a demonstrated track record of culturally sensitive and respectful, community-centered collaboration with Indigenous Peoples and local communities. Demonstrated ability to interact with Indigenous peoples and local community representatives, senior government, NGO, business, and donor staff. Experience with the Convention on Biological Diversity and/or other multilateral agreements and processes, focusing on biodiversity, Indigenous peoples’ and local communities’ rights, and finance. Experience delivering technical and financial reporting to donor agencies on large projects. Experience managing similar, complex, multi-stakeholder and multi-country projects. Experience leading a team of staff and coordinating sub-grant partners, ideally across multiple time zones and cultures. Technical experience and knowledge in the thematic area of the project, such as Indigenous -led territorial stewardship, community-based sustainable development, etc. Knowledge of the Open Standards for the Practice of Conservation, or WWF Project and Program Management Standards, preferred. Experience with GEF Projects and GEF knowledge an advantage. Written and spoken fluency in English required; advanced proficiency in Spanish, French, or Portuguese – highly preferred. Additional Information Location The position will be based in Brazil, Cambodia or Kenya. If applying to work in Brazil or Kenya, applicants must be nationals legally authorized to work in Brazil or Kenya. Employment visa sponsorship and relocation are not provided for Brazil or Kenya. PLEASE NOTE: If applying to work in Cambodia, nationals from South and Southeast Asian countries who are willing to relocate to Cambodia may also apply, and WWF-Cambodia may be able to support visa sponsorship and relocation costs based on available budget. Please note: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the job's location. Position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship. review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. UN Women in Georgia supports state and non-state partners towards the achievement of substantive gender equality in Georgia. In line with national and international commitments, UN Women works on the levels of policy and legislation, institutions and grassroots, in order to achieve transformative results for increased gender equality and greater protection of the rights of women and girls. UN Women puts special emphasis on the work towards gender mainstreaming in good governance reforms and enhancing women’s political participation, ending violence against women, promoting and supporting women’s economic empowerment, and Women, Peace and Security agenda. Along with these key priority areas that constitute UN Women’s mandate, UN Women interventions in Georgia are anchored in the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) in Georgia. Progress towards gender equality remains slow and uneven, while resistance to women’s rights continues to grow globally. The UN Secretary-General’s report Women’s Rights in Review 30 Years After Beijing [1] highlights that nearly one-quarter of governments worldwide reported a backlash against women’s rights in 2024. Similarly, The Gender Snapshot 2025 [2] , produced by UN Women and the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA), estimates that, at the current pace, gender parity in managerial positions will take nearly a century to achieve. These trends underscore the need for renewed efforts to challenge entrenched gender norms and accelerate progress towards equality. Engaging young people is critical to these efforts, as they can challenge stereotypes, shape public attitudes and drive social change. In Georgia, research suggests that younger generations generally hold more egalitarian attitudes than older groups on several aspects of gender equality. However, this progress cannot be taken for granted: traditional gender norms persist, while international evidence points to growing polarization among young people, particularly between women and men. Investing in youth engagement, critical thinking and leadership is therefore essential to equip young people with the knowledge, skills and confidence to challenge discrimination and advance gender equality. Against this backdrop and with the support of the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation (Norad), UN Women will be developing and conducting the Generation Equality Youth Lab. The Generation Equality Youth Lab is a flagship UN Women initiative designed as a five-day programme bringing together young people to explore gender equality, understand inequalities and discrimination, and examine the links between women’s empowerment and broader political, economic and social development. Through interactive learning, critical reflection, storytelling, debates and creative exercises, participants will explore how social norms, language, media and digital spaces shape attitudes and behaviours. The Lab will strengthen their critical thinking, communication and leadership skills, equipping them to challenge discriminatory attitudes, engage constructively with diverse perspectives and promote equality in their everyday environments. Ultimately, the initiative aims to cultivate a new generation of informed and confident gender equality champions who can mobilize their peers, build alliances and drive positive change in their communities and beyond. To support the development of the Generation Equality Youth Lab curricula, UN Women intends to engage a National Consultant. The National Consultant will report to the UN Women Programme Specialist and UN Women Project Analyst and will be supported by the UN Women Project Assistant, who will be the point of contact for contractual and payment matters. In close coordination and under the overall guidance of UN Women, the consultant will undertake the tasks outlined below. Integrate participatory and experiential learning approaches, including critical reflection, storytelling, group discussions, debates, role-play, case studies and creative exercises, to encourage active engagement, peer learning and the practical application of knowledge. Define measurable learning outcomes and assessment methods, including approaches to assess participants’ knowledge, skills and attitudes at the beginning and end of the programme, as well as opportunities for reflection on how participants can apply their learning in their communities. Integrate a practical component on youth-led initiatives and community action planning, enabling participants to identify opportunities to apply their learning, mobilize their peers and develop ideas for small-scale initiatives that promote gender equality in their communities. Consult with UN Women throughout the development process to review and refine the proposed programme structure, thematic content and ensuring alignment with the objectives and intended results of the Generation Equality Youth Lab. review_candidates.title: Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning Officer - HCI
review_candidates.description: Company Description Founded in 1961, WWF works to help people and nature thrive. As a global conservation organization, WWF operates in more than 100 countries, partnering with communities, companies, and governments to protect wildlife, conserve vital habitats, and advance sustainable solutions. Grounded in science and driven by collaboration, WWF works to help nature by conserving biodiversity, supporting resilient communities, and addressing climate change. Nearly 1 million people in the United States and more than 5 million globally are WWF members. Project Description The Heart of Conservation Initiative ( HCI ) is a 5-year global project designed to address systemic barriers that limit Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ ability to steward their lands, territories, waters, and biodiversity-rich ecosystems. Despite strong evidence that Indigenous Peoples and local communities manage or influence at least 37% of remaining natural lands globally, they receive less than 1% of international climate and biodiversity finance, face complex donor procedures, limited direct access to funding, and insufficient recognition in decision-making arenas. Building on the achievements of the GEF-7 Inclusive Conservation Initiative (ICI), HCI’s objective is to increase Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ organizational capacities and ability to access sustainable finance at scale for territorial stewardship to deliver social, economic, cultural, and Global Environmental Benefits. The project is transformative in that it targets structural change in biodiversity finance systems—shifting from centralized, intermediary-driven models toward more inclusive, Indigenous Peoples and local community-led financing and governance mechanisms. This will be achieved through four integrated components: (i) organizational and technical self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community funds and organizations and implementation of self-determined Indigenous Peoples- and local community-led sub-projects across Latin America, Africa, and Asia; (ii) collective self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community-led funds and organizations’ institutional, fiduciary, and technical capacities; (iii) enhancing Indigenous Peoples' and local communities’ representation and influence in global biodiversity and biodiversity finance processes; (iv) advancing knowledge, learning, and evidence on rights-based, inclusive conservation; and (v) monitoring and evaluation. Job Description Major Function Under the guidance and supervision of the Project Manager, the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer will be responsible for monitoring, evaluation, and learning activities including tracking and reporting project implementation, performance and results achieved – both for C1 partners and the Heart of Conservation Initiative (HCI) as a whole. This is a unique, cross-cutting role (with a focus on components 1 and 5) supporting monitoring of a global, Indigenous-led project that should respond both to Indigenous and local community partners’ priorities as well as GEF core indicator requirements. The MEL Officer will be responsible for the collection and analysis of data in relation to the project activities, outputs, outcomes and impacts; reflecting on and improving the results framework to align with the project theory of change, co-developing a learning agenda and approach, and respond to emerging learning needs and supporting adaptive management; assisting the Project Manager in preparing semiannual, and annual technical reports on project progress; and collaborating with the Communications and Knowledge Management Officer to support identification of impacts and lessons for public-facing communications. The MEL Officer will work in close collaboration with the Project Manager of the Global Coordination Unit (GCU), C1 and other implementing partners, as well as relevant organizations for data-sharing and data management. Key Responsibilities Collaborate with the Project Manager and C1 partners, as relevant, to design methodology for the collection of relevant indicators in close collaboration with all technical specialists. Monitor application of project M&E plans, gather and analyze data for reliability, precision, and feasibility, advising on solutions as needed; and guide usage of monitoring data for project adaptive management, learning needs and decision-making. Deliver a Results Framework and Work Plan Tracking Report for the global HCI at the end of each project year, including, as applicable; measurements against required Core indicators. Co-develop a learning agenda with C1 partners (Indigenous Peoples and local communities’ organizations) – with due focus on Indigenous Peoples and local community-led territorial stewardship and tenure security, Indigenous Peoples and local community-led financing models, women’s and youth leadership in Indigenous Peoples and local communities’ governance, and advocacy in biodiversity finance decision-making fora. Co-develop culturally appropriate learning methods to support the learning agenda and collaborate with project partners to capture lessons learned. Assist the Manager to write the 6-month and 12-month Project Progress Reports/Annual Project Implementation Report for the WWF-GEF Project, including progress, learning and reflections, adaptive management, outcomes, and project ratings. Proactively investigate and reflect on emerging data with C1 partners and GCU staff for adaptive management proposals. Lead planning and organization of the annual reflection workshop to reflect on monitoring data and experience, identify lessons related to the learning agenda and beyond, and inform adaptive management of the project and summarize them in workshop reports. Collaborate with the Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) and the Communications & Knowledge Management (CKM) Officers to organize and support learning exchanges and knowledge fairs that incorporate and respect traditional approaches to knowledge-sharing among project partners and other relevant parties with emphasis on engaging women and youth. Based on the results frameworks described above, work with the CKM Officer to design a transparent, live database that maintains project monitoring, evaluation and learning knowledge and data collected over the course of project implementation. Support management of said database to ensure data is accurate and updated, with guidance to ensure consistency of measurement methodologies over time. Collaborate with C1 partners and the CKM Officer to respect data sovereignty and address data safety risks through systems, protocols and agreements. Collect and analyze additional data relevant to project from external sources. Troubleshoot challenges with C1 and other partners, including to find culturally appropriate data collection solutions and Indigenous Peoples and local community-accessible reporting and documentation approaches. Contribute to external evaluation planning and execution, including co-design of terms of reference with the Project Manager, C1 partners and WWF GEF Agency, participation in data gathering, review of deliverables, and providing logistical and coordination support to evaluators. Support the Project Manager and CKM Officer to present the project's progress and lessons learned at appropriate regional and international forums. Week-long, international travel may be expected on an approximately quarterly basis. Any other tasks that are relevant to the assignment. Qualifications Key Competencies Demonstrated ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder projects and competing priorities. Analytical Attention to detail Collaborative Intercultural and adaptive management skills Reliability/follow-through Cross-cultural communication Skills And Abilities A Bachelor’s degree is required in natural or social science, environmental management, program evaluation, international development, adult/organizational learning, or a related field; an advanced degree preferred. At least 7 years of relevant work experience; a Master’s degree in the aforementioned fields will substitute for 2 years of experience. At least 3 of those years of experience must be in the design and implementation of M&E systems for development or conservation projects implemented by national/international NGOs/agencies/government or large, Indigenous associations. Experience supporting Indigenous peoples and local communities organizations with a demonstrated track record of culturally sensitive and respectful, community-centered collaboration with Indigenous Peoples and local communities required. Strong analytical skills/expertise in analyzing data, including expertise using database software, such as Excel or Smartsheet. Experience in research methods, designing and implementing tools and strategies for quantitative and qualitative data collection, analysis and production of reports. Experience using statistical software, such as R or Stata, is desired. Familiarity with the Open Standards for Conservation Management (or WWF Program and Project Management Standards) and results-based management principles, tools, and techniques is preferred. Familiarity with traditional ecological knowledge and biocultural indicators an asset. Experience organizing learning and/or capacity-strengthening events or exchanges, with prior experience supporting learning in international development or conservation an advantage. Strong writing skills and fluency in English required, with Spanish, French, and/or Portuguese fluency or working knowledge strongly preferred. Experience working in distributed teams, ideally across multiple time zones required. International, developing country field experience is preferred, especially in a monitoring and evaluation role in a development or conservation context. Additional Information Location: The position will be based in Brazil, Cambodia or Kenya. If applying to work in Brazil or Kenya, applicants must be nationals currently based and legally authorized to work in Brazil or Kenya. Employment visa sponsorship and relocation are not provided for Brazil or Kenya. If applying to work in Cambodia, nationals from South and Southeast Asian countries who are willing to relocate to Cambodia may also apply, and WWF-Cambodia may be able to support visa sponsorship and relocation costs based on available budget . Please note: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the job's location. Position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship.
